record.paper_title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions
record.original_question: Let (K_i)_{i\ge 1} be compact subsets of ℝ such that 0\in K_i for every i, every element of every K_i is nonnegative, \operatorname{diam}(K_i)>0 for all i, and \operatorname{diam}(K_i)	o 0. Define S={∑_{j=1}^∞ x_j\mid x_j\in K_j} and, for each z, define the tail set R_z={∑_{i=z+1}^∞ x_i\mid x_i\in K_i}. What topological spaces can S be homeomorphic to?

evidence.quote:
Instead, we list the following open questions:
1. What are the possible sets S can be homeomorphic to?

artifact.status_search_result: For the classical case where each $K_i = \{0, a_i\}$ (subsums of a null sequence of positive reals), it is known that the achievement set is either a finite union of closed intervals, a Cantor set, or a Cantorval, and there are continuum many non-homeomorphic Cantorvals. However, in the more general compact-set setting posed here, no full classification of the possible homeomorphism types of $S$ is known; the problem is listed as open in the originating survey, and no subsequent resolution was found in the literature search.

status_evidence.title: Cantorvals and Subsum Sets of Null Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Subsum sets of null sequences include finite unions of intervals, Cantor sets, and Cantorvals.
status_evidence.claim: Classical achievement sets fall into three families, but the broader compact-set version remains uncharacterized.

status_evidence.title: On compact subsets of the reals
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the structure of subsum/achievement sets of sequences of compact sets in the reals.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to investigate which compact subsets of ℝ arise as achievement sets, indicating no complete classification yet.
